name: Validator Dispatch (validators-and-failure-modes)
description: Activity-driven implementation of post-task validator dispatch per OpenSpec change 2026-04-26-validators-and-failure-modes (§7). Subscribes to lifecycle:task:completed and chains five tasks: (1) discover_validators — find activities consuming the parent task's outputShapes AND producing validation_result via the canonical `discoverByShapesQuery` impulse-resolve shape (mode=backward + output_shapes=[validation_result]); (2) select_validator_per_shape — pick a validator from the activity envelope using composition_score and Thompson α/β; (3) dispatch_validators — execute the chosen validator with the parent task's outputs as inputs; (4) propagate_failure_mode — when validation_result.passed === false, emit a failure_mode_propagation impulse carrying the structured verifier_negative failure_mode for the dispatcher to stamp on the parent trace; (5) learning_signal_write — record impulse_relevance + tool_argument_pattern signals for the parent task, gating executionSucceeded on validator outcome. As of 2026-04-26 the template uses dotted-path interpolation (e.g. {{lifecycle.taskId}}, {{lifecycle.executionId}}) — the interpolate regex was extended to /\{\{([\w]+(?:\.[\w]+)*)\}\}/g in iter 7 (activity.ts:6952). Task 1 uses the canonical `impulse-resolve` + `discoverByShapesQuery` pattern advertised by activity-api — zero minibob source changes (vessel-integration constraint).

variables.name: selectionMethod
variables.description: Selection strategy for producer_selection. 'deterministic' (default) picks highest mean (α/(α+β)) for reproducibility; 'thompson' Beta-samples each candidate. Mirrors slot-binding.json — deterministic is the safer default for first ship.

variables.name: lifecycle
variables.description: Set automatically by the lifecycle dispatcher (see activity.ts:1249-1273) to the lifecycle:task:completed payload merged with {executionId, shape}. Contains: taskId, taskIndex, executionId, status, outputShapes, durationMs, skip_validation, allImpulseIds, loadedImpulseIds, toolCallRecords. As of 2026-04-26, dotted-path interpolation works: `{{lifecycle.taskId}}`, `{{lifecycle.executionId}}`, `{{lifecycle.outputShapes}}` (array → JSON-stringified), `{{lifecycle.skip_validation}}` (boolean → string `"true"`/`"false"`), `{{lifecycle.allImpulseIds}}` (string[] → JSON-stringified), etc. Resolvers can also read the lifecycle:task:completed impulse content directly via `impulses` (delivered as the first impulseRef) for any field not surfaced as a dotted-path placeholder.

tasks.description: Find activities that can validate the just-completed task's outputs.
tasks.notes: Uses the canonical `discoverByShapesQuery` shape — activity-api advertises this shape via discovery-vessel, and the existing generic `impulse-resolve` resolver in minibob dispatches the request with no source changes in the integrating vessel. Posts mode=backward + required_shapes={{lifecycle.outputShapes}} + output_shapes=[validation_result], which finds activities that CONSUME the parent task's outputs AND PRODUCE validation_result. Specialized validators (whose input_shapes literally contain one of the parent's output shapes) win over wildcard validators implicitly via the same shape filter. SHORT-CIRCUIT: when the parent task sets `skip_validation: true` on its config, the lifecycle:task:completed payload forwards that flag; the conditional below skips this task — and the rest of the chain via dependency-skip propagation — so no shape query, validator dispatch, or learning-signal write occurs. When `skip_validation` is omitted or false the conditional evaluates true and the chain runs as before.

tasks.description: Reshape the discoverByShapesQuery result (a plain {activities, total} envelope) into a variant_selection_result-formatted memo so the downstream `activity` resolver (task 3) can pi…

prompt.template:
You are converting a discoverByShapesQuery result into a variant_selection_result impulse for the downstream activity dispatcher.

Input envelope (JSON): {{impulse:discover_validators_result}}
The envelope's `content` field (when delivered as the impulse-resolve response) is a JSON-stringified {activities: Activity[], total: number}. Each Activity has `id`, `name`, `output_shapes`, `input_shapes`, and may have `metrics` (Thompson α/β, success_rate) and `composition_score` ({alpha, beta} when mode=candidates_with_scores; null otherwise).

If total === 0 OR activities is empty, output: {"selected":null,"unbindable":true,"reason":"no validator candidates returned by discoverByShapesQuery"}

Otherwise pick the BEST candidate by:
1. If any candidate has composition_score (non-null), maximise composition_score.alpha / (composition_score.alpha + composition_score.beta).
2. Else maximise metrics.thompson_alpha / (metrics.thompson_alpha + metrics.thompson_beta).
3. Tie-break by metrics.total_executions DESC, then by `id` lexicographically.

Output EXACTLY (no markdown, no prose):
{"selected":{"activity_id":"<winner.id>","template_id":"<winner.id>"},"runner_ups":[{"activity_id":"<id>","template_id":"<id>"}, ...],"selection_method":"composition_score_or_thompson","unbindable":false}

No other fields. No commentary.

tasks.notes: Reshape the discoverByShapesQuery result (a plain {activities, total} envelope) into a variant_selection_result-formatted memo so the downstream `activity` resolver (task 3) can pick up the chosen validator's activity_id via its existing extractSelectedActivityId path (activity-resolver.ts:41). Now selects from the canonical shape result rather than producer_selection_result — the LLM picks a winner using composition_score (when present) and Thompson α/β as tiebreakers. The spec describes per-shape partitioning (specialized vs wildcard) which isn't expressible in the current template format (no foreach over outputShapes); the validator's own inputShapes filter at dispatch time enforces the specialization implicitly. FUTURE CLEANUP: when a deterministic `impulse_reshape` resolver lands, replace this LLM call with `(activities → top by composition_score · α/(α+β))` selection.

tasks.description: Execute the chosen validator activity with the parent task's outputs as the validator's inputs.

variables._dispatch_note: Validator activity receives the parent task's outputs via the inherited impulse pool — the lifecycle subscriber merge path (activity.ts:1249-1273) already merges output impulses from the parent task's outputShapes into this nested execution's input pool. No explicit variable plumbing needed.

tasks.notes: Reads the variant_selection_result emitted by task 2; ActivityResolver.extractSelectedActivityId pulls selected.activity_id and loads the validator template via loadTemplateFromMCPOrLocal (cache → MCP → embedded). The validator activity executes its own task chain and emits validation_result impulse(s). SIMPLIFICATION: dispatches a SINGLE validator (the one task 2 picked); multi-validator dispatch is deferred. There is no fallback template — when task 2 reports unbindable=true the conditional skips this task entirely. If a malformed variant_selection_result slips through, ActivityResolver returns an error impulse rather than dispatching a sentinel activity.

tasks.description: When the dispatched validator emitted at least one validation_result with passed=false, build a failure_mode of type 'verifier_negative' and emit a failure_mode_propagation impulse…
tasks.notes: When the dispatched validator emitted at least one validation_result with passed=false, build a failure_mode of type 'verifier_negative' and emit a failure_mode_propagation impulse for the dispatcher to stamp on the parent task's trace metadata. NO ACTIVITY-API ENDPOINT EXISTS TODAY for writing trace metadata mid-execution — the proper wiring is Phase 5 of the OpenSpec change (activity.ts:5454-5529 inline path replacement), which lifts failure_mode handling out of the executor. Until Phase 5 lands, we emit the structured failure_mode as an impulse and rely on the lifecycle subscriber merge path to surface it in the parent execution's impulse pool, where downstream learning_signal_writer (task 5) and any post-execution observers can read it. The conditional expression follows the slot-binding.json idiom (line 162 of goal-processing-activity-driven.json: `{{impulse:...}} contains '<literal substring>'`) — we substring-match `passed":false` in the dispatch_validators_result impulse content. The validator activity is expected to emit at least one validation_result impulse whose JSON content contains either passed=true or passed=false per the unified contract (spec §3.1).

tasks.description: Record per-task learning signals (impulse_relevance + tool_argument_pattern) for the parent task that just completed.

config._lifecycle_note: taskId/templateId/executionId/allImpulseIds/loadedImpulseIds/toolCallRecords use dotted-path interpolation against the lifecycle:task:completed payload. The interpolator JSON-stringifies array values when embedded as string leaves of resolver config; the resolver tolerates JSON.parse-able string-form arrays so the chain wires end-to-end. templateId is in the lifecycle payload. The hardcoded 'executionSucceeded: false' is a deliberate conservative default — the meta-activity fires post-completion specifically when validation may have failed; the parent task's intrinsic success is irrelevant to the validation-success signal. A future cleanup wires this to the validator's pass/fail outcome.

tasks.notes: This is the migration target for the three executor call sites (`activity.ts:5471, :5574, :5719`); once Phase 5 deletes those, the meta-activity owns all learning-signal writes. executionSucceeded gates how Thompson Sampling α/β eventually update — when the validator reported a failure (validation_result.passed=false somewhere), executionSucceeded should be FALSE even though the parent task's lifecycle.status was 'completed'. SIMPLIFICATION: the executionSucceeded determination ideally inspects the dispatch_validators_result impulse contents; without dotted-path interpolation OR a dedicated flag-extraction resolver, we delegate it to the resolver itself. The lifecycle:task:completed payload carries `allImpulseIds`, `loadedImpulseIds`, and `toolCallRecords` (activity.ts:2407 + :2877 emit sites); the learning_signal_writer resolver tolerates JSON-stringified array forms so dotted-path interpolation (which JSON-stringifies array values when embedded as string leaves of resolver config) feeds through correctly. templateId is carried on the lifecycle payload and forwarded via {{lifecycle.templateId}}. The learning_signal_writer resolver no-ops gracefully on missing/empty templateId rather than throwing — learning signals are best-effort.

metadata.author: validators-and-failure-modes
openQuestions: Per-shape iteration: the spec's task 2 (select_validator_per_shape) ideally partitions candidates per produced shape into specialized (input_shapes literally contains the shape) vs wildcard (input_shapes: ['*']) and dispatches the right validator per shape. The current template format has no foreach/map primitive (infra gap B), so this template models the single-validator, single-shape-of-validation case. The validator's own inputShapes (enforced by matchImpulsesForTask at dispatch time) acts as the specialization filter implicitly. Multi-shape, multi-validator dispatch is a follow-up.

Architectural correction: instead of registering a thin `discover_by_shapes` resolver in minibob (which would have edited minibob source to call activity-api — a violation of the pure-vessel/vessel-integration constraint), activity-api advertises a `discoverByShapesQuery` shape via its impulse-resolve handler (repos/activity-api/src/routes/impulses.ts). The shape's pointer carries the same fields as the REST route body (required_shapes, mode, output_shapes, current_shapes, limit, predecessor_activity_id) and the handler delegates to the same shared helper (services/discover-by-shapes.ts) as the REST route. This template's task 1 (discover_validators) uses the canonical pattern: existing `impulse-resolve` resolver + `pointer.type: "discoverByShapesQuery"` with mode=backward + output_shapes=[validation_result] — zero minibob source changes.

producer_selection_result → variant_selection_result format adapter (task 2): the LLM prompt is mechanical and could be replaced with a deterministic `impulse_reshape` resolver (or a `variant_selection_from_producer_selection` resolver). Until then the LLM call is a low-cost placeholder — keep maxTokens=400.

failure_mode propagation mechanism (task 4): no activity-api endpoint exists today for writing trace metadata mid-execution. The Phase 5 cleanup (spec §8) is where failure_mode handling moves from inline activity.ts code into structured impulses. This template emits failure_mode_propagation as an impulse; the lifecycle subscriber merge path surfaces it in the parent execution's impulse pool. Downstream consumers (trace storage, dashboard) read it from there. Once Phase 5 lifts the inline path, the impulse-based propagation becomes authoritative.

executionSucceeded for task 5: hardcoded to false because the meta-activity fires post-completion to capture validator outcomes, and the parent task's lifecycle.status doesn't reflect validator pass/fail. Once a flag-extraction primitive exposes the dispatch_validators_result impulse content as a derived variable, this becomes `true if all validation_results passed, else false`. Dotted-path interpolation alone doesn't suffice (we'd need an `{{impulse:dispatch_validators_result.passed_aggregate}}` capability or a deterministic reshape resolver).

templateId is included in the lifecycle:task:completed payload (activity.ts:2429 + :2899 emit sites) and consumed via {{lifecycle.templateId}} in task 5's config. The learning_signal_writer resolver no-ops gracefully on missing/empty templateId rather than throwing — learning signals are best-effort and missing data should not break the meta-activity. The chain (allImpulseIds/loadedImpulseIds/toolCallRecords/templateId) is wired end-to-end.
limitations: Single-validator dispatch (task 3): multi-validator parallel dispatch is deferred until template foreach lands.
executionSucceeded hardcoded to false in task 5 — conservative default; refines once a flag-extraction primitive over impulse content lands (see openQuestions).
metadata.subscriberContract: subscription.shape = 'lifecycle:task:completed'. Fires after every task's loop iteration AND every parallel-group entry (activity.ts:2429, :2899). Lifecycle payload: { taskId, templateId, taskIndex, executionId, status, outputShapes, durationMs, skip_validation, allImpulseIds, loadedImpulseIds, toolCallRecords }. The dotted-path interpolator JSON-stringifies array values when embedded as resolver-config string leaves; the learning_signal_writer resolver tolerates JSON-stringified array forms. Subscriber outputs (validation_result, failure_mode_propagation, learning_signal_write_result) merge back into the parent execution's impulse pool via the existing nested-execution machinery (activity.ts:1249-1273).
metadata.outputContract: Per shape-provenance principle (2026-04-27): each task's declared outputShapes is the UNION of possible emissions — actual emissions depend on conditional gates. (1) discover_validators emits validator_candidates iff skip_validation !== true; (2) select_validator_per_shape emits variant_selection_result + selected_validators iff candidates exist; (3) dispatch_validators emits validation_result/validation_results + activityExecutionSummary iff a validator was selected (unbindable=false); (4) propagate_failure_mode emits failure_mode_propagation iff at least one validation_result reported passed=false; (5) learning_signal_write always emits learning_signal_write_result. Impulses carry shapeOrigin: 'validator_emitted' (set by the resolvers via metadata) so trace consumers can stratify validator-driven shapes from resolver-emitted ones. Downstream consumers gating on `validation_result` see it ONLY when a validator was actually dispatched — not as a phantom shape from a skipped task.
